subject: tech
title: Plan It Out
about: Before building a program, a game or a drawing, programmers make a plan: a goal, the steps, and what they expect at the end, sometimes as a storyboard of little pictures (K2-AP-05). The cards find the goal of a plan, spot a missing step, predict the result, check the result against the plan, and then change the plan and say what changed and why, which is the iterative process in K2-AP-08. Read it together and plan something real afterwards, like a block tower or a paper airplane.
tip: Before his next block tower, ask him to say the goal, the steps, and what it will look like, then check the finished tower against the plan.

cards.q: You want to make a game on the tablet. Which comes first, planning it or building it?
cards.note: Plan first, build second. A plan says the goal, the steps and what should happen.

cards.q: A plan has a goal, the steps, and the ending you expect. Which part is the list of things to do?
cards.note: The goal is what you want and the steps are how. The ending is what you expect to see.

cards.q: Plan: get flour, mix, bake, frost. What is the goal of this plan?
cards.note: The goal is the thing you want at the end. Every step points at it.

cards.q: Plan: get a pot, add dirt, drop in a seed, water it. What is the goal?
cards.note: Read the steps and ask: what are they all for? That is the goal.

cards.q: Plan: draw a house, color it, add a sun. What do you expect to see at the end?
cards.note: Saying what you expect before you start is part of the plan.

cards.q: Your plan says: the robot rolls to the door, then beeps. What do you expect at the end?
cards.note: Predict first, then run it. If the robot beeps at the door, the plan worked.

cards.q: Before making a video, you draw little pictures of each part in order. What is that called?
cards.note: A storyboard is a plan made of pictures. Movie makers use them too.

cards.q: Your storyboard shows: puppet waves, puppet sings, puppet bows. Which part do you film first?
cards.note: A storyboard goes in order, left to right. The first picture is the first thing you film.

cards.q: Plan: open the drawing app, pick blue, save the drawing. Which step is missing?
cards.note: You cannot save a drawing you never drew. Check a plan for missing steps.

cards.q: Your plan said a red house. Your drawing shows a blue house. What do you do next?
cards.note: Checking the result against the plan shows you what to fix.

cards.q: You compare your drawing with your plan and they match. What does that mean?
cards.note: A match means your plan worked. Now you can share it or make the next plan.

cards.q: Your paper airplane plan made a plane that fell straight down. What do you do to the plan?
cards.note: Changing a plan that is not working is smart. Programmers do it all the time.

cards.q: You changed your plan and now the plane flies. A friend asks how. What do you tell your friend?
cards.note: Say what you changed and why: I made the wings wider because it fell fast.

cards.q: You made the wings wider because the plane fell fast. Which part is the why?
cards.note: The why is the reason for the change. Saying it helps you remember what works.

cards.q: Plan, build, test, fix, and go round again. What is this round-and-round way of working called?
cards.note: Iteration means going round again, a little better each time. Say it: it-er-AY-shun.

cards.q: Which one of these is a plan?
cards.note: A plan is steps that lead to a goal, with a guess about what happens at the end.

cards.q: Your guess about what will happen at the end of your plan has a name. What is it?
cards.note: A prediction is a careful guess. Make one, then test to see if it comes true.
